content.intro: Target rating points (TRPs) measure how much of a schedule lands on the people you actually want to reach, such as women 25–54 or recent SUV intenders, rather than a broad demo. They use the same math as GRPs, but against your target audience. This calculator works out TRPs from reach and frequency, turns TRPs into target impressions, and prices a schedule from your cost per point.
content.quick_answer: **TRPs = reach in your target audience (%) × average frequency.** Reaching 50% of your target an average of 4 times is **200 TRPs**. One TRP is 1% of the target audience, so **target impressions = TRPs ÷ 100 × audience size**.
content.how_it_works: The formula is **TRPs = target reach (%) × average frequency**, the same as GRPs but measured only against your target audience. 50% target reach at an average frequency of 4 is 200 TRPs. Because one rating point is 1% of the audience, **impressions = TRPs ÷ 100 × target audience size**: 200 TRPs against a 40 million target is 80 million target impressions. To price a schedule, **cost = TRPs × cost per point**. A schedule usually delivers more GRPs than TRPs, because some of its impressions fall outside your target.

faq.question: What is the difference between TRP and GRP?
faq.answer: GRPs measure exposure against a broad demographic such as adults 18+. TRPs measure exposure against your specific target, such as women 25–54 with household income over $100K. The math is the same, **reach × frequency**, but TRPs only count people in your target, so they're the better guide to whether a schedule reaches who you want.

faq.question: How do you calculate TRPs from GRPs?
faq.answer: Multiply GRPs by the share of the schedule's audience that is in your target. If a schedule delivers 300 GRPs among adults 18+ and 40% of those impressions reach your target, it delivers about **120 TRPs**. Your measurement partner's target ratings give the exact figure.

faq.question: How do you turn TRPs into impressions?
faq.answer: One TRP is 1% of your target audience, so **impressions = TRPs ÷ 100 × audience size**. 150 TRPs against a 20 million target audience is 30 million target impressions.

faq.question: How many TRPs do I need?
faq.answer: Use the same ranges planners use for GRPs, applied to your target: sustaining campaigns often run 150–250 per 4-week flight and launches 300–500. Below about 100 it's hard to move brand metrics. Check the reach and frequency behind the total, not just the points.
